niche: an intergovernmental liability risk pool setting its 2027 per-occurrence retention from the ground-up severity of its members' liability occurrences, which the pool sees only above each member's deductible and records only up to its own limit
answer: Keep the first $4,000,000 of each 2027 liability occurrence: Fallowmere's 2027 retention is the $4.0 million quoted attachment, which the pool expects 0.74 of its 2027 occurrences to cost more than (1.25 above $3.0 million)

spine.entity: one liability occurrence the pool handled (above its member's deductible), with the member's deductible and the pool's paid and reserved amounts

world.geography: United States (a fictional intergovernmental risk pool of Washington cities and special districts)
world.org_type: intergovernmental risk pool of cities and special districts

driver: The decisive quantity is the upper tail of a size distribution whose items reach the record only above a floor that differs from item to item and are recorded only up to a ceiling that moved during the record, and whose largest items stay unfinished long after the small ones finish; the fit has to carry each item's floor as truncation and the ceiling as censoring at the fitted cost level over every item of the window, the unfinished ones included as the censored observations they are, because fitting only the finished items selects on size and thins the tail a step short, and fitting the recorded sizes as complete thins it more.
driver_concrete: Ground-up liability severity is fitted at 2027 cost to every occurrence of accident years 2014 to 2021 in the pool's record (800 closed and 20 suits still open while the excess insurer defends them, each with the pool's layer paid), each occurrence left-truncated at its member's deductible and the 108 that reached the retention right-censored there, both at 2027 cost; the expected 2027 occurrences above each quoted attachment first fall to one at $4.0 million, while the same fit on the closed files alone clears one at $3.0 million and the lognormal fitted to the closed files' costs as complete at $2.0 million.
stump: The default path keeps the closed occurrences of 2014 to 2021, whose costs are final, brings each recorded ground-up cost to 2027 cost and fits the policy's lognormal by maximum likelihood as a complete sample, which thins the tail and ends on $2.0 million; censoring the 88 closed occurrences stopped at the retention ends on $2.5 million; carrying each deductible as truncation as well, both thresholds at 2027 cost, still ends on $3.0 million (0.70 above it) because the 20 open suits, every one past the retention, were set aside; the same fit on every file of the window files $4.0 million (1.25 above $3.0 million, 0.74 above $4.0 million).
analyst_test: A strong analyst who reads every field and every filed rule, keeps the closed files of 2014 to 2021 for their final costs, brings each to 2027 cost and fits the policy's lognormal by maximum likelihood to the recorded ground-up costs files $2.0 million, with the occurrences at the retention censored files $2.5 million, and with each deductible as truncation as well still files $3.0 million, because the open suits it set aside are a fifth of the occurrences that reached the retention.
domain_test: The call turns on the ground-up severity distribution of liability occurrences, estimated the way loss models are fitted to insurance data observed through deductibles and policy limits (a truncated and censored likelihood with each observation's own thresholds at the fitted cost level) over a claims record whose largest files settle last, and on its tail at each quoted attachment; with another field's nouns there is no deductible below which losses never reach the record, no retention at which they stop being recorded, no excess insurer defending the suits past it, and no excess attachment to set.
